scenario.summary: Threat actors are leveraging AI-driven penetration testing frameworks like ARTEX and PentAGI to automate reconnaissance, credential spraying, and post-exploitation at machine speed. These frameworks orchestrate a variety of offensive tools including C2 frameworks (VShell, AdaptixC2), tunneling utilities (Chisel, NPS), and internal scanners (fscan) to rapidly compromise targets across both endpoint and cloud environments.

hunt.name: ARTEX Automated Endpoint and Network Maneuvering
hunt.description: ARTEX and similar agentic frameworks coordinate worker agents to deploy offensive toolsets at machine speed. This hunt identifies the execution of common binaries used by these agents—including VShell, Chisel, and fscan—and correlates them with behavioral indicators of automated network scanning and unauthorized module loads into LSASS. By examining these signals across process, network, and module telemetry, an analyst can distinguish between a human operator and an objective-driven automated framework.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, process_original_file_name, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{offensive_tools}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{offensive_tools}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_original_file_name) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify hosts executing binaries associated with ARTEX worker agents to narrow the search space.
config.expected_signal: Rows indicating the execution of known offensive tools. Silence suggests no direct matches for the named binaries occurred.

primitive_config.label: Offensive Tool Execution Lead
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, process_original_file_name, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{offensive_tools}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{offensive_tools}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_original_file_name) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Rows indicating the execution of known offensive tools. Silence suggests no direct matches for the named binaries occurred.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, COUNT(DISTINCT dst_endpoint_ip) AS unique_targets, COUNT(*) AS total_conns FROM hb_network_connection WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name HAVING unique_targets > 15 ORDER BY unique_targets DESC
config.description: Detect automated internal scanning by finding processes that contact a high volume of unique internal destination IPs.
config.expected_signal: Processes (like fscan or vshell) that target dozens of internal hosts in a short window. Genuine admin tools may show this, but rare process names should stand out.

primitive_config.label: Network Discovery Prevalence
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, COUNT(DISTINCT dst_endpoint_ip) AS unique_targets, COUNT(*) AS total_conns FROM hb_network_connection WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name HAVING unique_targets > 15 ORDER BY unique_targets DESC
primitive_config.expected: Processes (like fscan or vshell) that target dozens of internal hosts in a short window. Genuine admin tools may show this, but rare process names should stand out.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, module_path, module_signature_subject, time FROM hb_module_activity WHERE (LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\lsasrv.dll' OR LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\samlib.dll') AND NOT (LOWER(process_name) LIKE 'c:\windows\system32\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE 'c:\windows\syswow64\%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Corroborate tool execution by finding module loads related to LSASS or SAM access from non-system directories.
config.expected_signal: Any row where a user-space binary is interacting with the credential databases. Silence proves the tools did not attempt LSASS memory access within the window.

config.objective: Determine if the execution of offensive tools, the high-velocity network connections, and the LSASS module loads together indicate an automated AI-enabled framework like ARTEX on any single host.
config.description: Assess whether the observed tools and behaviors indicate an automated framework coordination.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict identifying malicious orchestration.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious, suspicious, or benign per host, citing the offensive binary name and connection volume.

config.question: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one host involving an offensive tool binary
config.condition: the triage verdict is malicious for at least one host involving an offensive tool binary
config.description: Direct the hunt to containment or manual review.
Disrupt the automated agent's planner by isolating the host.
config.instructions: Isolate the host and terminate any processes identified by the triage agent as malicious.

config.description: Confirm the findings and assess for the presence of the agent harness.
config.instructions: Review the process ancestry for the offensive binaries; search for unusual Python or Node.js processes that may be acting as the ARTEX agent harness coordinating the tools.

config.description: Document findings and ensure EDR health across the fleet.
config.instructions: Record the outcome and verify that all hosts in the affected segment have reporting EDR agents, as ARTEX frameworks often include bypass capabilities.
